fiscal.source: CBO August Monthly Budget Review (09-09): $2.0tn deficit over the first 11 months of FY2026, consistent with the ~5.8% full-year projection. CRFB puts the 12-month rolling deficit at ~5.5% of GDP. Debt/GDP 122.6% is the Q1-2026 GFDEGDQ188S print

sentiment_changes: Fed: hold 3.50-3.75%; August payrolls +162k vs 56k expected, unemployment 4.1% (09-04) -> hold 3.50-3.75% ahead of the 09-16 meeting; August core CPI +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected

sentiment_snapshot.note: Baseline roster as developed in conversation. Week 1 diffs against this file. scripts/build_report.py copies it to data/sentiment_current.json on first run and updates that file thereafter; this baseline is never overwritten.

fed.name: Fed / Warsh
fed.stance: hold 3.50-3.75% ahead of the 09-16 meeting; August core CPI +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected
fed.read: hike near-certain: CME September odds ~85%, up from ~70% before CPI

roster.name: Yardeni
roster.note: Held: Warsh more hawkish than expected, but 1-2 hikes don't derail the target
roster.statement_summary: 'US MARKET CALL: Warsh Proof': keeps YE 8,400 (forward EPS $415 x 20.2); 10y still in a 4-5% 'normal-for-longer' range

roster.name: Wood
roster.note: Held: rotation within megacaps (out of GOOGL, into META), not de-risking
roster.statement_summary: ARK sold ~$28.7M of Alphabet (09-09/09-11) and bought ~$27.9M of Meta

roster.name: Lee
roster.note: 8,000 near-term target BUT explicitly warns of bear-market-like moves Aug-Oct
roster.statement_summary: S&P to 7,900-8,000 this month ('the bigger the base, the bigger the breakout'), year-end 8,000+ with upside to 8,400-8,800 - while flagging four H2 triggers

roster.name: Siegel
roster.note: Held: expects a hike, a 'shudder' and sell-off, then a range-bound market
roster.statement_summary: CNBC Closing Bell: Warsh will 'bite the bullet and raise rates'; 'you'll see a sell off'

roster.name: Sonders
roster.note: Held: correction-level drawdowns tend to come within 12 months of a first hike; slow cycles are milder
roster.statement_summary: Schwab 'Take a Hike: Rate Hikes and Market Impacts': fast-cycle average drawdown ~-16% vs ~-12% for slow cycles

roster.name: Druckenmiller
roster.note: CUT and GAP CLOSED: reportedly cut AI holdings to ~20% of their level six months earlier (FT, via secondary source), calls AI a likely 'profit bubble' and rates too low
roster.statement_summary: Piper Sandler closed-door meeting (FT): Fed members calling policy restrictive are 'just ridiculous'; 'We are likely in a profit bubble because this AI construction boom will eventually end'

roster.name: Roubini
roster.note: RAISED from +1: not worried about an AI bubble; rising real yields reflect AI capex and growth, not a bond crisis
roster.statement_summary: Cernobbio interview (Bloomberg video 'Roubini Says He's Not Concerned About an AI Bubble'): stocks rise with growth, though 'some corrections' possible

roster.name: Slok
roster.note: 12m cut to 0: frames early 2027 as AI succeeds or fails - in the failure case the Nasdaq could fall 50%
roster.statement_summary: Daily Spark 'Think Six Months Ahead': long rates much lower in six months either way; AI failure means rotation out of equities

roster.name: El-Erian
roster.note: Conviction up: more bond-bearish, AI market path getting bumpier; no explicit equity call
roster.statement_summary: CNBC at Cernobbio: global bond sell-off not over; 'I don't see any appetite in the U.S. for immediate fiscal consolidation'

roster.name: Gross
roster.note: 'No crash, just a forward weave requiring a cane'; bearish long Treasuries on deficits, prefers energy infrastructure and MLPs to exuberant tech
roster.statement_summary: Valuation casts a shadow over 2026; the record rally is at risk of stalling unless AI earnings show up

roster.name: Buffett-Berkshire
roster.note: REVEALED PREFERENCE FLIPPED: first net buying in 15 quarters. Cash still $365bn, so the caution is real - but the direction of travel reversed
roster.statement_summary: Q2-26: ~$19.8bn net equity purchases after 14 straight quarters of net selling; cash $397.4bn -> $365.5bn; $4.5bn of buybacks; Alphabet now the third-largest holding at $36.6bn

roster.name: Marks
roster.note: current worry is private credit, not public equity: fast capital deployment into direct lending, with PE portfolio-company performance as the hinge
roster.statement_summary: Memo 'What's Going On in Private Credit?' - direct lending's growth, and the issues rapid deployment created

roster.name: Dimon
roster.note: 12m cut to -3, but the rhetoric>action gap stands: JPM keeps lending and underwriting while he says he would not buy
roster.statement_summary: 'Margin debt is the highest it has ever been', much of it hidden in prime brokerage, ETFs and Treasury-basis trades; says he would not buy the S&P 500 or long-dated Treasuries at today's prices and the market is one bad trade from panic selling

roster.name: Krugman
roster.note: Held: Fed commentary, no equity view
roster.statement_summary: Yahoo Finance interview: Warsh's speech 'utterly conventional' - 'tight money until we see a lot better data'

roster.name: Dalio
roster.note: conviction up: says his own indicators already put AI stocks in bubble territory, and the next crisis is sovereign rather than banking
roster.statement_summary: Late-stage debt cycle; Fed balance-sheet expansion is 'stimulus into a bubble'; most likely path is a 1970s-style stagflationary spiral with the Fed monetising

roster.name: Rosenberg
roster.note: conviction up: says credit markets are already writing the warning - directly relevant to the HY tripwire
roster.statement_summary: With Richard Bernstein: the AI trade is a bubble, real disposable income is fractionally negative y/y, and ex-AI the four-quarter real GDP trend is under 1.5% - a K-shaped economy where profits take all the income growth

roster.name: Grantham
roster.note: latest sourced statement is June 2026 - inside the 6-month window but not fresh this fortnight
roster.statement_summary: Calls this 'the most expensive market in American history'; a reversion to trend would be closer to a wipeout than a correction, and the odds an AI bubble does not bust are 'slim to none'

roster.name: Burry
roster.note: Scion stopped filing 13Fs in Nov 2025 - positions now come from his Cassandra Unchained Substack, so the disclosure lag is his choice and the newest trades (Aug 4) are paywalled
roster.statement_summary: Disclosed bearish book: puts on NVDA and PLTR at up to ~80% of the portfolio (~$1.1bn notional), plus TSLA, CAT, AMAT, SMH and MU opened 30 June and added 24 July
